overview: Lassa fever is an acute viral illness caused by Lassa virus that was first identified in 1969 in Nigeria. The virus belongs to the virus family Arenaviridae. Lassa fever is a zoonotic disease, meaning that humans become infected from contact with infected animals. The animal reservoir, or host, of Lassa virus is a rodent of the genus Mastomys, commonly known as the multimammate rat.
symptoms: Bleeding from the mouth, nose, vagina or gastrointestinal tract
transmission: Humans may also become infected directly via contact with infected rats.
risk_factors: Contact with food or household items contaminated with rodent urine or faeces
complications: Bleeding from the mouth, nose, vagina or gastrointestinal tract
